correctness.rationale: The centered cumulative-cut indicators form the positive gap decomposition of every increasing finite score. Their exact covariance matrix gives the least normalized ray correlation at the first and last cuts. The positive bilinear covariance expansion plus the L2 triangle inequality yields the claimed universal lower floor. Strictness, boundary sharpness, the correlation-one equality case, and interval filling are all reconstructed analytically.

value.rationale: Ordinal categories admit many legitimate order-preserving numerical codings, and Pearson correlation is sensitive to spacing. The theorem gives the exact worst-case agreement between any two such codings from the category-frequency profile alone, identifies the extremal endpoint-collapse mechanism, and yields a simple 1/(m-1) benchmark under equal frequencies.
